assertion.uniformity: Formation is compatible with base change.
assertion.normalizations: The factors correspond to field embeddings.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The endomorphism-lattice field, Tate faithfulness and ramification conclusions remain separate.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the restriction and product decomposition before deriving the induced Tate representation and inertia action.

use.reason: Apply the accepted finite-separable Weil restriction theorem to the projective surface. Base change to Qbar gives the product indexed by embeddings; functoriality transports factors under Galois. The subsequent Tate direct sum and inertia argument is the explicit local application in main1214–1223.
use.shared_contract_justification: Both occurrences concern the same W0, K and A: initial construction and its later conjugate-product realization.

assertion.statement: Shapiro identifies the actual finite-level class with the integral group-basis coefficient module used in K10, compatibly with the unnormalized transition maps.
assertion.objects: The original fixed T_2E, actual cyclotomic finite levels, inverse-deck group-ring coefficients and specified inertia subgroups in K7/K10.
assertion.hypotheses: The actual finite-level classes, integral module maps and their norm compatibility are supplied by the preceding construction. U is open, the coefficient is a discrete continuous U-module; for the permutation model it extends to a G-module. The stated commuting deck action uses U normal.
assertion.quantifiers: All groups, modules and degrees in the stated source scope.
assertion.parameter_range: The indicated section of the published2006 Selmer Complexes.
assertion.uniformity: Functorial cohomological maps; no arithmetic bound is asserted.
assertion.normalizations: Original Tate lattice, arithmetic Frobenius and inverse deck action; no division by a group order.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This application does not construct the Euler-system classes, prove the Kato norm relation, or provide a uniform bound on higher cohomology. Only the stated cochain/coefficient comparison is imported.
assertion.limit_order: Use the discrete finite coefficient statement before a separately justified inverse limit, except for4.1.3 which explicitly supplies that inverse-limit sequence.

use.reason: Apply at each finite coefficient precision to the open normal cyclotomic subgroup. Section8.1.3 gives the integral permutation basis. Section8.1.6.3 identifies the commuting deck action by hU->h*g^(-1)U, exactly the inverse-deck convention after naming that group basis. The explicit Phi_n in K10 is then checked on that basis in the manuscript; Shapiro does not itself assert equivariance of an arbitrary weighted map. Section8.1.6.2 gives unnormalized coset projection for corestriction, not division by the index.

supplier.statement: For an open subgroup U of a profinite group G, evaluation at1 gives a quasi-isomorphism from continuous cochains with induced discrete coefficients to cochains of U; the induced module has the explicit permutation-module model, and corestriction corresponds to the coset projection.

use.reason: Take the continuous homomorphism to be the inertia inclusion and U the cyclotomic subgroup. Its preimage is upper inertia; the finite cosets enumerate the primes above the given place. The source decomposition and commuting restriction diagram identify the local restrictions with the upper restrictions. A zero class therefore stays zero under the integral coefficient map Phi_n. The finite local decomposition introduces no character projector or index denominator.

supplier.statement: Restriction of an induced coefficient module along a continuous homomorphism decomposes over the finite cosets of the induced image, and the Shapiro maps commute with the resulting local restriction maps up to the specified homotopy.
